summary: Clarify why tool-invoke tariff was applied to scheduled batch embedding job (customer believes embed-only)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a scheduled nightly embedding job (daily batch) was charged at the higher 'tool-invoke/chat' rate on 2026-03-08 03:00 UTC. The job has historically been charged using the embed rate. The customer asserts no tool calls were in the payload and that the job configuration pins the embed-only model.

Impact:
- Unexpected charge of ~$420 on March invoice line item for one nightly run (Maple Health Tech account).
- Customer is on Dedicated plan and uses reserved capacity; they rely on predictable unit economics for budgeting.
- Customer requests provisional credit and root-cause explanation; they flagged this as high priority due to month-end reconciliation.

Environment:
- Account: maple-health-prod (dedicated pool)
- Region: us-west (hosted fallback disabled for this tenant)
- Job: daily-embed-job-2026-03 (Airflow schedule)
- Model pinned: redwood-embed-v2@v2026-02-18
- Invocation method: async batch via /v1/embeddings.batch endpoint (internal orchestrator)

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Trigger the same Airflow DAG with identical input file used on 2026-03-08.
2) Observe job execution logs in the customer's orchestrator and Redwood request logs.
3) Verify the API usage line items in billing export for the run's time window 2026-03-08T03:00:00Z - 03:20:00Z.

Attached logs/IDs:
- Customer provided sample request IDs: req_9f48b2c1, req_9f48b2d7, req_9f48b2f4 (from their side).
- Billing line item id: invline_20260308_8421
- Customer upload: batch_manifest_20260308.csv (attached to ticket)

Initial hypothesis from Support: 
- Possible classifier mislabeling where mixed-model batch or tool-invoke flag set at router level; or a transient model fallback to a chat-capable variant that carries the tool-invoke tariff.
- Alternatively, postback/rate-lookup cache may have been stale and returned chat rate for embed model id during that 20-minute window.

Requested by customer:
1) Provisional credit for the single run (amount estimate provided by customer: $420).
2) A postmortem explaining root cause and steps to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:13 - Aisha Patel: Acknowledged receipt. Asking billing team to apply provisional credit while we investigate. Submitted billing export request for 2026-03-08 02:50-03:30 UTC window.

2026-03-10 14:02 - Miguel Torres: Investigating. Pulled router logs for the customer's dedicated pool around the window. There are three requests that matched the customer's request IDs. Router shows 'route_variant: embed-only' but a downstream substitution to model 'redwood-chat-compat@v2026-02-01' occurred for one request due to tokenization error (fallback). Raising with serving-runtime on-call to confirm why fallback happened for an embed batch.

2026-03-11 08:21 - SRE (on-call): Found a transient key-error in the tokenizer service causing the embed model scorer to return 500 for a small subset of inputs; the router's fallback policy is configured to route to a compatible chat-capable variant for resiliency. That variant is tariffed under tool-invoke/chat pricing. We are collecting the exact tokenization exception traces and will post them to the ticket.

2026-03-11 12:40 - Miguel Torres: Noted. Reached out to product to confirm whether fallback should have used a 'compatible embed variant' rather than chat-capable one for customers on dedicated pools that disable hosted fallback. Product says routing policy had an override deployed on 2026-03-06 that mistakenly enabled cross-variant fallback for pools with older config. Creating INT ticket to get override reverted and adding a guard to prefer embed-formattable fallbacks.

2026-03-12 09:05 - Customer (Maple Health Tech): Thanks for the updates. We'd like provisional credit and also to know if we need to pin a different setting on our Airflow job to avoid this. We do not want chat-capable fallbacks for embed runs.

2026-03-12 11:34 - Miguel Torres: We will recommend a config flag you can set on the DAG to enforce 'no-cross-variant-fallback' for embed batches and will provide the CLI snippet. Also requested provisional credit from billing for the $420 line item; billing needs confirmation from eng that this was a platform fallback event.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Router logs show 3 customer request IDs; 2 were served by redwood-embed-v2 as expected; 1 request hit tokenizer exception (ValueError: invalid byte sequence) and router applied fallback policy to redwood-chat-compat which has tool-invoke tariff.
- Tokenizer error originated from a malformed record in the customer's manifest (one line contained unexpected null bytes); the customer file included binary artifact.
- Config mistake: a routing override (deploy id override-20260306) changed fallback precedence for dedicated pools; intended to be a temporary canary but selector matched some legacy dedicated pool configs.
- Billing system correctly applied the chat tariff for that single request; however, the invoice line was aggregated and rounded up, producing the $420 charge for the run.

Pending actions:
- Revert override-20260306 in routing config (INT-7722) - done 2026-03-12 09:18 UTC.
- Add server-side guard to prefer embed-compatible fallback variants for embed endpoints; tracking as INT-7788.
- Provide customer CLI config to set 'enforce_embed_only: true' on batch jobs; sample provided in comment.
- Billing provisional credit: requested; awaiting approval from billing ops.
resolution: Pending billing provisional credit. Engineering root cause identified (tokenizer exception + routing override). Revert performed and guard created as follow-up. Once billing confirms provisional credit, ticket will be set to Resolved. Customer provided with recommended manifest sanitization steps and a config flag to enforce embed-only behavior.
resolution_notes: Provisional credit request submitted to Billing Ops with evidence bundle (router logs, tokenizer trace, invoice line). Billing ticket BOT-5591 created. Engineering remediation: revert confirmed; follow-up INT-7788 to implement fallback guard.
next_steps: 1) Billing Ops to confirm provisional credit application (BOT-5591). 2) Engineering to implement fallback preference guard (INT-7788) and schedule postmortem. 3) Customer to sanitize manifests and optionally set 'enforce_embed_only' on the DAG. 4) Close ticket after credit is applied and customer acknowledges.
customer_requested_action: Provisional credit and guidance to prevent chat-fallback for embed batches
